gaps: Can the fix be verified without real Windows?
What's the most likely root cause of exit 1 vs expected 2/0?
resolutions: No — .cmd cannot run off Windows; the windows-hook-gates CI job is the sole verifier (user chose CI iteration). The change must be reason-complete and self-consistent about cmd.exe semantics.

The tests rely on cwd-shadowing of py/python/python3 but the subprocess inherits the runner's full PATH, so interpreter resolution is nondeterministic; and/or forge.cmd's fallback chain can reach a run_python* label that execs a failed interpreter (exit 1) instead of routing to :missing (exit 2). Fix both: make tests set PATH to only the stub dir + System32, and make forge.cmd's exit routing correct.
notes: FORGE-WIN-2.6 fixes three real-Windows forge.cmd exit-code failures on PR #83; verified via CI.
